articles.title: The Rook Board: Meowth makes me choose the athlete
articles.dek: Seviper owns the strongest grade band. Central Sinnoh’s Meowth owns the movement tests. Calvin Rook ranks twelve receivers from a group of twenty-one.
articles.author: calvin-rook

body.text: Central Sinnoh’s Meowth is my first receiver. Celadon’s Seviper has the stronger present grade band, and I expect plenty of sensible scouts to prefer him. I am taking the 4.71 forty, 43-inch vertical and 6.27 cone seriously enough to put the athlete first. This is a scouting opinion with an obvious argument against it. Keep both parts of the sentence.

This week’s circuit covers the twenty listed WRs and one SLOT, with twelve prospects on the board. Grades remain ranges; combines describe the workout. They do not tell us a receiver’s college production, guarantee an evolution or promise a future starting job. The useful question is which actual assignment a team would be buying.

Rustboro just received an eighteen-yard touchdown from Gengar. Saffron survived because Venomoth finished a 69-yard pass. Those plays explain why teams keep looking for receiving threats. They do not make every prospect of a related species the next version of an established player. I want a fit, a price and a job before I want a comparison that sounds good on draft night.

prospects.name: Meowth
prospects.analysis: I am putting Central Sinnoh’s Meowth first, and I know exactly which objection is coming: the 41–69 grade band is lower than several others. The movement testing wins me over. A 4.71 forty, 43-inch vertical and 6.27 cone are the best marks in this receiver group. That is the athlete I want to investigate first when I need a receiver to create space.
prospects.concern: Ten bench reps do not settle how he handles contact, and the broad grade band leaves real uncertainty about present receiving polish.
prospects.projection: My first receiver target for Fortree, whose 0–5 start demands a stronger offensive future. This is a fit opinion, not a forecast of its draft slot.

prospects.name: Seviper
prospects.analysis: Seviper offers the strongest current grade band here at 62–90 and nineteen bench reps. Celadon’s prospect gives a club a different reason to be interested than Meowth does: there is a stronger present evaluation range and a much sturdier strength result. I would be entirely comfortable with a team reversing my top two because it values that combination more.
prospects.concern: The 4.95 forty and 6.87 cone trail the leading movement testers. The strongest band is still a band, not a completed scouting report.
prospects.projection: A receiver-needy club wanting a more immediate contribution should start here. I would put Cerulean on the list after its three-point afternoon.

prospects.name: Gastly
prospects.analysis: Sycamore’s Gastly pairs a 4.82 forty with a 6.53 cone and a 41-inch vertical. The 57–85 band belongs near the top, too. I like how little explaining is required to make the movement case. Think about the stress a receiver can place on a defense when it must respect both the initial acceleration and a change of direction.
prospects.concern: Four bench reps are the clearest weakness in the testing profile. Movement alone does not establish dependable receiving or blocking work.
prospects.projection: A serious early option for a team seeking another explosive receiving threat. Rustboro has just shown how useful a Gengar can be, without making that an automatic comparison of ability.

prospects.name: Delibird
prospects.analysis: Hulbury’s Delibird has a 56–84 grade band, a 41-inch vertical and a 6.62 cone. I see a balanced candidate to challenge for real receiving work rather than a workout attraction with one number doing all the selling. The 4.92 forty does not lead the class, but the other movement tests keep the profile interesting.
prospects.concern: Eight bench reps and a broad band leave work to do on the contact and present-skill questions. Do not turn a good jump into an invented catch history.
prospects.projection: A sensible receiver addition for an offense that already has one dependable option and needs another. Pewter should be looking at more ways to reach the end zone.

prospects.name: Chinchou
prospects.analysis: The only listed SLOT in this group belongs high enough to be discussed on his own terms. Azalea University’s Chinchou has a 56–84 band, runs 4.87 and posts a 6.70 cone. A club that has a real inside receiving job can consider those numbers without pretending every receiver has to solve the same outside assignment.
prospects.concern: A 36-inch vertical and ten bench reps do not distinguish him from every outside prospect. The role must exist before the selection makes sense.
prospects.projection: My first call for a team specifically shopping for inside receiving work. I would ask Lavender to define that job before adding another target to a crowded idea of an offense.

prospects.name: Woobat
prospects.analysis: Woobat matches Gastly’s 41-inch vertical and 6.53 cone, with a 4.87 forty. The Icirrus prospect is 23 and level 23, carrying a 46–74 band. The test results justify a close look even though the present grade range sits below the leading group. I would rather discuss those specific strengths than dismiss the profile because it starts sixth.
prospects.concern: Seven bench reps and the lower grade band remain meaningful differences from stronger present candidates. Age 23 also gives less age-based runway than 21.
prospects.projection: A middle-board receiver to compare against actual openings, particularly for teams wanting movement help soon. I would keep him in Fortree’s comparison even if Meowth is unavailable.

prospects.name: Delibird
prospects.analysis: Lavaridge’s Delibird has the same 4.92 forty as Hulbury’s, with a 6.66 cone and eleven bench reps. The differences are the 42–70 band and 36-inch vertical. I like a prospect who keeps several useful measurements together. Being 21 is another reason to consider the longer view, provided a club can actually give him a useful development place.
prospects.concern: Level seven and the lower band make immediate starting assumptions unwise. A younger age does not award a future breakthrough.
prospects.projection: An option for a club building a receiving succession plan while retaining its current starter. Mossdeep has productive veterans and can afford to compare future jobs carefully.

prospects.name: Spinda
prospects.analysis: Gateon’s Spinda is my favorite of the four Spinda profiles in this group. The 4.90 forty, forty-inch vertical and 6.65 cone form the strongest movement combination among them, with thirteen bench reps as well. The 38–66 band is a reason to keep evaluating, not a reason to pretend the athletic differences are invisible.
prospects.concern: The band still reaches well below an assured starting standard. He must be compared as a whole player rather than selected because this is the best Spinda workout.
prospects.projection: A development-minded receiver target when the price reflects uncertainty. I would put him in Mossdeep’s longer-term comparison rather than promise an immediate role.

prospects.name: Spinda
prospects.analysis: Lavender Forest’s Spinda brings a 41–69 band and a 6.71 cone, but the five-second forty is slower than Gateon’s. There is a defensible argument for taking the stronger present band first. I lean the other way because I want the broader athletic package, and I am leaving this entry beside Gateon’s so that argument remains easy to have.
prospects.concern: At 23, there is less reason to pay a premium merely for youth. Nine bench reps and a 37-inch vertical do not separate him from the middle of the board.
prospects.projection: A receiver-needy team should compare the current evaluation directly with Gateon’s. A later selection makes more sense to me than reaching because the top of the band looks comfortable.

prospects.name: Spinda
prospects.analysis: I enjoy discussing Dewford University, and this Spinda gives me a respectable excuse. At 21, with a 37–65 band, a 38-inch vertical and a 6.80 cone, he belongs in the next group of developmental comparisons. I cannot honestly call the 4.95 forty exceptional. I can say the profile has more than one usable measurement.
prospects.concern: Eight bench reps and an uncertain current grade require a patient role. The university name is not a football skill, even when I like saying it.
prospects.projection: A later receiver option for a team with room to develop him. Fortree needs help, but it also needs to avoid confusing a pleasant school connection with readiness.

prospects.name: Ekans
prospects.analysis: Mesagoza State’s Ekans has a 38–66 band, a 4.95 forty and a 6.73 cone. Those numbers keep him close to the Spinda cluster. Eleven bench reps give him a useful strength result within that group. I would bring him into the comparison whenever the preferred receivers are gone and a club still has a specific job to fill.
prospects.concern: He is 23 and level six. Neither the band nor the 35-inch vertical supports a promise of immediate high-end receiving production.
prospects.projection: A later developmental option with a defined job, not a generic collection piece. Cerulean should compare him with the alternatives before assuming any receiver automatically fixes the offense.

prospects.name: Spinda
prospects.analysis: Fuji University’s Spinda closes the twelve with a 34–62 band, 4.98 forty and 6.77 cone. The cone time is close enough to the surrounding group to keep the discussion open. Ten bench reps and a 37-inch vertical complete a profile that needs a favorable price and a clear developmental purpose rather than a dramatic sales pitch.
prospects.concern: The lower end of the grade range is a substantial warning. I would not turn the similarities in testing into a claim that the receivers are interchangeable.
prospects.projection: A late comparison candidate for a club that can preserve a useful roster place. I would prioritize more complete receivers before making room for another uncertain project.

art.alt: Football, agility cones, stopwatch and clipboard at a dawn workout.
